home.title: Sermon Studio: from a service recording to sermon files
home.description: Sermon Studio turns the recording of a church service into sermon files: cut the sermon out on a waveform, and get evenly loud FLAC, MP3 and Opus.
home.h1: From the recording of a service to sermon files
home.lede: Sermon Studio runs in the browser. Upload the recording of the whole service, mark where the sermon starts and ends, and press Save. You get the sermon as FLAC, MP3 and Opus, at an even, standard loudness, ready for a podcast or the church's website.
home.hero.alt: The editor: the service as a waveform, with the sermon marked
home.video.note: The video is in English, without sound.
home.video.fallback: Your browser cannot play this video. Download it (MP4).
home.how.intro: Five steps, each in the studio as the pictures show it.
home.step1.p: Drop the recording of the service on the recordings page, or choose it. Most audio and video files work: WAV, FLAC, MP3, M4A and more. The date is taken from the file name. A recorder can also drop its files in a folder, or a sound technician can send them with a code, without a login.
home.step1.alt: The recordings page: by year, with status and labels
home.step2.p: The whole service is shown as a waveform. Drag across the sermon, or move its start and end. Cut out a cough or a song in the middle. Listen to the joins before you save. The original recording is never changed.
home.step2.alt: The editor: the sermon in two sections, with a cough cut out
home.step3.p: Processing sets mono or stereo, noise reduction, leveling and the loudness. The church's defaults are used until you change them. An intro and an outro, such as a jingle and a closing word, can go around the sermon, at the same loudness.
home.step3.alt2: Intro and outro: the church's intro before the sermon
home.step4.p: Save keeps the edit and makes the files you chose. You can follow the work, or close the browser: it goes on without you.
home.step4.alt: Save: the files are made, step by step
home.step5.p: The finished files are on the recordings page, with the intro and outro or the sermon only. Share for download gives a code and a link, so someone without a login can download the sermon.
home.step5.alt: The finished files in the Download menu
home.step5.alt2: Share for download: a name, which files, how many downloads, an end date
home.what.1: Even loudness. The sermon is noise-reduced, leveled and brought to podcast loudness (−19 LUFS), measured with EBU R128.
home.what.2: The original is kept. Files are only deleted after their copy has been checked to be identical.
home.what.3: Several churches. Each church has its own recordings, members, tags, logo, intro and outro.
home.what.4: On a phone too. In English, Norwegian bokmål and nynorsk, light or dark.
home.churches.p1: Do you record your services and want the sermons online? Write to contact@sermon-studio.app with the name of your church. We set up the church in the studio and send you a link to log in. You then invite the others who will use it.
home.churches.p2: Would you rather run it yourself? Sermon Studio is free and open source. Run it on your own server with Docker (how), or use the desktop app below on one computer.
home.churches.p3: Read how the studio is used in the guide, and what is stored in privacy.
home.download.p1: The desktop app runs the studio on one computer, without a server or a login. It is for Windows, macOS and Linux, and has everything it needs built in.
home.download.unsigned: The app is not signed, so Windows and macOS warn the first time you start it. On Windows, choose More info, then Run anyway. On macOS, open System Settings → Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway. After that it starts like any other program. Each release lists the checksum of every file.
guide.title: Guide: using Sermon Studio
guide.description: A short guide to Sermon Studio: uploading, marking the sermon, processing, intro and outro, saving and sharing.
guide.lede: A short tour, in the order you meet it. The pictures show a real speech: President Kennedy's inaugural address (1961), uploaded as a WAV.
guide.recordings.p: All the church's recordings, by year. to do means not cut yet; done means saved, with files. The search finds names, dates and labels. Click a row to play the sermon, download it or add labels.
guide.upload.p: Drop a file at the top of the page, or choose one. The date is taken from the file name or the file; change it if needed, and give the recording a name if a day has two. The upload goes in parts, so it goes on after a dropped connection. It then opens in the editor.
guide.upload.alt: The upload form, with the date from the file name
guide.edit.p1: The editor shows the whole service as a waveform. Silences are grey. A new recording starts with the sermon set to all of it but the silence at its start and end.
guide.edit.p2: Sections are what you keep: drag their edges, or set the start and end at the playhead. Drag on an empty part of the waveform to add another section; what is between sections is left out. Cuts take a part out of a section, such as a cough or a song. Each can have a label. Hear join plays a join as it will sound.
guide.edit.p3: Your changes are kept as you go, also if you close the page. Undo and Redo are in the bar at the bottom.
guide.edit.alt: The editor: two sections, with a cough cut out of the second
guide.processing.p: How the sermon is made into files: mono or stereo, noise reduction, how much of the room's sound to keep, leveling, compression and the loudness. Hear a sample makes 30 seconds to listen to first. A recording starts with the church's defaults, set in Settings → Processing.
guide.processing.alt: The Processing step in the editor
guide.clips.p: Upload the church's clips in Settings → Intro and outro, and choose the default intro and outro. In the editor, each sermon can use the default, another clip, none, or a clip of its own. The clips are brought to the sermon's loudness, with a short pause at each join. With an intro or outro, the sermon on its own is made too.
guide.clips.alt: The Intro and outro step in the editor
guide.save.p: Choose the formats under Output: FLAC, MP3 and Opus. Save keeps the edit, then makes the files that are missing or out of date. The work goes on if you close the browser. A file made from an older edit says out of date on the recordings page.
guide.files.p: On the recordings page, a sermon's Download button lists its files, with their sizes: with the intro and outro, or the sermon only. A format not made yet can be made from there.
guide.files.alt: The Download menu of a finished sermon
guide.share.p1: Share for download… on a finished sermon makes a code and a link. Someone without a login can then download it. You choose the files, and if you want, how many downloads and an end date.
guide.share.p2: The other way works too: under Shares (the icon in the header), make a code that lets someone send recordings to the church without a login, such as the sound technician.
guide.share.alt2: The public page, opened with the link
guide.more.p: The full guide, with every detail, is on GitHub (in English). Questions: contact@sermon-studio.app.
privacy.title: Privacy: Sermon Studio
privacy.description: What Sermon Studio stores, where, who processes it, how long it is kept, and how to have it deleted.
privacy.lede: What the hosted studio at app.sermon-studio.app stores, where, who processes it, how long it is kept, and how to have it deleted. If you run Sermon Studio yourself, or use the desktop app, everything stays on your own server or computer, and none of this reaches us.
privacy.site.p: This website sets no cookies and has no tracking, analytics or adverts. It loads nothing from other sites. Your browser remembers the language you choose here, and nothing else. The website is served by Cloudflare, which sees your IP address in order to deliver the pages.
privacy.login.p: You log in through a login provider. The studio keeps the provider's ID for you, and the name and email address the provider gives. The name and email are only shown to the admins of your churches; they are never used to give access. While you are logged in, your browser has a session cookie, and the studio keeps a hash of it and the token from the login, so that it can log you out at the provider too.
privacy.members.p: For each church: who its members are and whether each is an admin. Invite links are kept only as a hash, with their expiry. Each church has its name, logo, default tags, processing, and intro and outro clips.
privacy.recordings.p: The recordings you upload, and the files made from them. With each recording: the edit (sections, cuts, labels, tags, processing), when it arrived, how each file was made, and when the latest change was made. A waveform and a listening preview are kept in a cache, to make the editor fast.
privacy.shares.p: A share is a code that lets someone without a login send recordings to a church, or download a sermon. The studio keeps a hash of the code, its settings, and for each upload or download: the file name, its size, the IP address and the time. The church's members see this list.
privacy.logs.p: The studio logs what it does: recordings received, files made, renamed and deleted, and changes to churches and members. For the public share page, it logs the IP address of uploads, downloads and wrong codes, to stop abuse. It does not log which pages you look at.
privacy.browser.p: The session cookie while you are logged in (30 days), and a short-lived cookie while you log out. Local storage keeps your language, theme and a few view settings, the church you last used, and the undo steps of the last 20 recordings you edited. Nothing in your browser is used for tracking.
privacy.where.p: On servers in the EU region. The recordings are not used for anything but making the church's files.
privacy.who.p1: Each church decides what it uploads and who its members are. Sermon Studio stores and processes it on the church's behalf. It is not sold, and not used for anything else.
privacy.who.p2: Processed for us by: the hosting provider (servers in the EU region), the login provider (your login), and Cloudflare (delivering this website and the studio's traffic).
privacy.kept.1: Recordings and files: until the church deletes them. A deleted recording stays in the church's trash for 30 days, then it is removed for good. The original can also be deleted on its own, once the files are made.
privacy.kept.2: The cache: removed after about 30 days without use.
privacy.kept.3: Shares: until they are removed. An ended share is removed after 30 days, unless the church chooses 7, 90 or 365 days, or never. Its list of uploads and downloads goes with it.
privacy.kept.4: Sessions: 30 days, or until you log out.
privacy.kept.5: Your login: until you ask us to delete it. Leaving a church, or being removed from it, ends the membership at once.
privacy.delete.p1: A church's admins can delete recordings (on the recording's page, then Settings → Trash → Delete now to remove it at once), remove members and remove shares. A member can leave a church in Settings → Members.
privacy.delete.p2: To have your login, or all of a church's data, deleted, or to see what is stored about you, write to contact@sermon-studio.app.
